questions.text:
मानव में अवायवीय श्वसन प्रक्रम से संबंधित कुछ अभिलक्षणों की सूची प्रवीन को निम्न तालिका के रूप में दी गई :

अवस्थिति: (i) पेशी कोशिका | परिस्थिति: (ii) ऑक्सीजन (O2) तथा कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड (CO2) की उपस्थिति की आवश्यकता | अंत्योत्पाद: (iii) 3-कार्बन अणु

उपर्युक्त अभिलक्षणों में से कौन-सा/से अभिलक्षण उपर्युक्त प्रक्रम से संबंधित है/हैं ?
questions.text_english:
Pravin was given a list of characteristics associated with the process of anaerobic respiration in humans, in the table given below:

Location: (i) Muscle Cell | Condition: (ii) Requires presence of Oxygen (O2) and Carbon dioxide (CO2) | End Product: (iii) 3-Carbon molecules

Which of the above characteristics is/are related to the above process ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) — (i) and (iii). Anaerobic respiration in humans occurs in muscle cells (i), making (i) correct. The end product of anaerobic respiration in humans is lactic acid, a 3-carbon molecule (iii), making (iii) correct. Option (ii) is incorrect because anaerobic respiration does not require oxygen — in fact, it takes place in the absence of oxygen. Therefore, options (i) and (iii) correctly describe the location and end product of anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है — (i) तथा (iii)। मानव में अवायवीय श्वसन पेशी कोशिकाओं में होता है, इसलिए (i) सही है। इसका अंत्योत्पाद लैक्टिक अम्ल है जो 3-कार्बन अणु है, इसलिए (iii) सही है। (ii) गलत है क्योंकि अवायवीय श्वसन में ऑक्सीजन की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।

questions.text: नीचे दिए गए चित्र का प्रेक्षण कीजिए तथा इस कार्यकलाप के संयोजन में गलत चरण की पहचान कीजिए :
questions.text_english: Observe the figure given below and identify the incorrect step for the activity set-up :

options.A: दोनों पौधों को शीशे के अलग-अलग जार में रखने से पहले तीन दिनों तक अँधेरे कमरे में रखा।
options.B: दोनों पौधों को अलग-अलग लकड़ी के बेल-जार से ढक दिया।
options.C: जार के तलों को सील करने के लिए काँच पट्टिका लगा कर वैसलीन का उपयोग किया।
options.D: मंड की उपस्थिति के लिए आयोडीन परीक्षण करने से पूर्व कुछ घंटों के लिए दोनों पौधों के गमलों को सूर्य के प्रकाश में रखा।

options_english.A: Both plants are kept in the dark room for three days before placing them in separate glass jars.
options_english.B: Both plants are covered with separate wooden bell-jars.
options_english.C: Use vaseline to seal the bottom of the jars with the glass plates.
options_english.D: Both potted plants were kept in sunlight for a few hours before the iodine test for the presence of starch.

questions.image_description: Two bell-jar setups are shown. Setup (I) shows a potted plant inside a glass bell-jar with a watch-glass containing potassium hydroxide at the base, sealed with vaseline and a glass plate. Setup (II) shows a similar potted plant in a glass bell-jar but without potassium hydroxide. The diagram illustrates an experiment to demonstrate the requirement of CO2 for photosynthesis.
questions.solution: The incorrect step is (B) — covering the plants with wooden bell-jars. The correct procedure requires glass bell-jars (not wooden ones) so that light can pass through and the experiment for photosynthesis can be conducted properly. Wooden bell-jars would block light, preventing photosynthesis from taking place. All other steps — destarding the plants in the dark, sealing with vaseline, and keeping in sunlight before the iodine test — are correct procedures for this photosynthesis activity.
questions.solution_hindi: गलत चरण (B) है — लकड़ी के बेल-जार का उपयोग करना। सही प्रक्रिया में काँच के बेल-जार चाहिए ताकि प्रकाश प्रवेश कर सके। लकड़ी के जार प्रकाश को रोक देंगे।

questions.text: सीधी रेखा में चलना तथा साइकिल चलाना जैसे क्रियाकलाप मस्तिष्क के कौन-से भाग के समन्वय के कारण संभव होते हैं?
questions.text_english: Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle are activities which are possible due to coordination of which part of the brain ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — Hind-Brain and Cerebellum. The cerebellum is a part of the hind-brain and is responsible for maintaining posture, balance, and precise coordination of voluntary movements. Activities like walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle require fine motor coordination and balance, which are controlled by the cerebellum. The cerebrum (forebrain) is involved in thinking and decision-making, while the medulla controls involuntary actions like heartbeat and breathing.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है — पश्चमस्तिष्क और अनुमस्तिष्क। अनुमस्तिष्क शरीर का संतुलन, मुद्रा और सटीक समन्वय बनाए रखता है। सीधे चलना और साइकिल चलाना इसी के नियंत्रण में आते हैं।

questions.text: एक अंतर्ग्रथन (सिनेप्स) में, रासायनिक संकेतों का संचरण होता है:
questions.text_english: In a synapse, the chemical signal is transmitted from :

options.A: एक तंत्रिका कोशिका के द्रुमिका सिरे से दूसरी तंत्रिका कोशिका के तंत्रिकाक्ष के अंतिम सिरे तक।
options.B: उसी तंत्रिका कोशिका के तंत्रिकाक्ष से कोशिका काय तक।
options.C: उसी तंत्रिका कोशिका के कोशिका काय से तंत्रिकाक्ष के अंतिम सिरे तक।
options.D: एक तंत्रिका कोशिका के तंत्रिकाक्ष के अंतिम सिरे से दूसरी तंत्रिका कोशिका के द्रुमिका सिरे तक।

options_english.A: Dendritic end of one neuron to axonal end of another neuron.
options_english.B: Axon to cell body of the same neuron.
options_english.C: Cell body to axonal end of the same neuron.
options_english.D: Axonal end of one neuron to dendritic end of another neuron.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) — from the axonal end of one neuron to the dendritic end of another neuron. At a synapse, the electrical impulse reaches the axon terminal (axonal end) of the first neuron, which triggers the release of chemical neurotransmitters into the synaptic cleft. These neurotransmitters then bind to receptors on the dendrites (dendritic end) of the next neuron, thus transmitting the signal. Option (A) is incorrect as it reverses the direction. Options (B) and (C) describe intra-neuronal signal movement, not synaptic transmission.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। एक सिनेप्स में रासायनिक संकेत एक तंत्रिका कोशिका के तंत्रिकाक्ष के अंतिम सिरे से न्यूरोट्रांसमीटर के रूप में निकलता है और दूसरी तंत्रिका कोशिका के द्रुमिका सिरे पर जाता है।

questions.text: उच्चतर पोषी स्तर के जीव जो निम्नतर पोषी स्तर से संबंधित अनेक प्रकार के जीवों को खाते हैं, मिलकर बनाते हैं:
questions.text_english: Organisms of a higher trophic level which feed on several types of organisms belonging to a lower trophic level form the :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) — Food web. When organisms at a higher trophic level feed on several different types of organisms from lower trophic levels, the multiple interconnected feeding relationships form a food web. A food chain is a single, linear sequence of who eats whom. An ecological pyramid represents the number, biomass, or energy at each trophic level. An ecosystem is the entire community of living organisms and their physical environment. Only a food web correctly describes the complex, interlinking network formed when one organism feeds on many different organisms.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है — आहार जाल। जब एक उच्चतर पोषी स्तर का जीव निम्न पोषी स्तर के कई जीवों को खाता है, तो परस्पर जुड़ी आहार श्रृंखलाएँ मिलकर आहार जाल बनाती हैं।

questions.text: किसी पारितंत्र में आहार श्रृंखला के माध्यम से उच्चतर पोषी स्तर में हानिकारक (विषैले) पदार्थों के संचयन में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-से जीव सर्वाधिक प्रभावित होते हैं?
questions.text_english: In accumulation of toxic substances at higher trophic levels of an ecosystem through the food chain, which of the following organisms is affected the most ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) — Human beings. This phenomenon is called biological magnification (biomagnification). Toxic substances like pesticides and heavy metals are not broken down and accumulate in the body fat of organisms. As we move up each trophic level, the concentration of these toxins increases significantly. Human beings occupy the highest trophic level in most food chains and therefore accumulate the maximum concentration of toxic substances. Small aquatic plants and small fish have lower concentrations because they are at lower trophic levels.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है — मानव। जैविक आवर्धन (Biomagnification) के कारण प्रत्येक उच्चतर पोषी स्तर पर विषाक्त पदार्थों की सांद्रता बढ़ती जाती है। मानव सबसे उच्च पोषी स्तर पर होने के कारण सर्वाधिक प्रभावित होते हैं।

questions.text: अंगूर के पौधों में प्रतानों की वृद्धि निम्नलिखित के कारण होती है:
questions.text_english: The growth of tendrils in grapes plants is due to :

options.C: अवलम्ब (आधार) के संपर्क में आई प्रतान (प्ररोह) कोशिकाओं में त्वरित कोशिका विभाजन
options.D: अवलम्ब संपर्क की सतह से विपरीत (परे) प्रतान (प्ररोह) कोशिकाओं में त्वरित कोशिका विभाजन

options_english.C: Rapid cell division in tendril cells in contact with the support
options_english.D: Rapid cell division in tendril cells that are away from the support

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) — Rapid cell division in tendril cells that are away from the support. The coiling of tendrils in grape plants is due to thigmotropism. When a tendril touches a support, the cells on the side touching the support divide slowly, while the cells on the side away from the support divide rapidly. This differential growth rate causes the tendril to curl around the support. This is a contact-based tropism (thigmotropism) and is not caused by light or gravity.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। अंगूर के प्रतानों की वृद्धि स्पर्शानुवर्तन के कारण होती है। आधार से दूर वाली कोशिकाओं में तेज़ कोशिका विभाजन होता है जिससे प्रतान आधार के चारों ओर कुंडलित हो जाता है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : सूक्ष्मजीवों की अनुपस्थिति में मृदा की प्राकृतिक पुन:पूर्ति नहीं होगी।
कारण (R) : जीवाणु तथा कवक जैसे सूक्ष्मजीव जीवों के मृत अवशेषों तथा अपशिष्ट उत्पादों का अपघटन (अपमार्जन) करते हैं, और ये मृदा (मिट्टी) में चले जाते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Natural replenishment of soil will not take place in absence of microbes.
Reason (R) : Microbes, comprising of bacteria and fungi, break down dead remains and waste products of organisms, and they go into the soil.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है। इन प्रश्नों के सही उत्तर नीचे दिए गए कोडों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से चुनकर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Select the correct answer from the codes (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) — Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The assertion is true: without microbes, the natural replenishment (nutrient cycling) of soil would stop. The reason is also true and directly explains the assertion: bacteria and fungi decompose dead organic matter and waste products of organisms, releasing minerals and nutrients back into the soil. This decomposition is essential for the renewal of soil fertility. Since the reason correctly and directly explains why the assertion holds true, option (A) is correct.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। सूक्ष्मजीव मृत पदार्थों को अपघटित करके पोषक तत्व मृदा में वापस पहुँचाते हैं, इसलिए उनके बिना मृदा की पुन:पूर्ति नहीं होगी।

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) — Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not correctly explain the Assertion. The assertion is true: the glomerulus in the kidney, like the alveoli in the lungs, is a cluster of very thin-walled blood capillaries, which facilitates filtration/exchange. Therefore, the reason is true but does not explain the assertion, making (B) correct.

questions.text:
(i) ओजोन परत के अवक्षय के लिए क्लोरोफ्लुओरोकार्बनों (CFCs) को मुख्य कारक माना गया है। 1987 में, संयुक्त राष्ट्र पर्यावरण कार्यक्रम (UNEP) में सर्वानुमति बनाने में सफलता मिली। इस सर्वानुमति का उल्लेख कीजिए।
(ii) हमारे वायुमंडल में ओजोन की क्या भूमिका है?
questions.text_english:
(i) Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) have been linked to depletion of ozone layer. In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) succeeded in making an agreement. State this agreement.
(ii) What is the role of ozone in our atmosphere ?

key_points: (i) The Montreal Protocol — an international agreement to freeze production of CFCs at 1986 levels and phase them out completely.
(ii) Ozone absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun, protecting living organisms on Earth from its damaging effects such as skin cancer and DNA damage.

questions.solution: In 1987, the United Nations Environment Programme succeeded in forging the Montreal Protocol, under which nations agreed to freeze the production of CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons) at 1986 levels and then progressively phase them out entirely, since CFCs were identified as the main cause of ozone layer depletion. The role of ozone in our atmosphere is to absorb harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation coming from the Sun before it reaches the Earth's surface. Without this ozone shield, UV radiation would cause serious harm to living organisms, including skin cancer, cataracts, and damage to plant and aquatic ecosystems.
questions.solution_hindi: 1987 में संयुक्त राष्ट्र पर्यावरण कार्यक्रम ने मॉन्ट्रियल प्रोटोकॉल के तहत सर्वानुमति बनाई, जिसमें CFCs के उत्पादन को 1986 के स्तर पर रोककर धीरे-धीरे समाप्त करने पर सहमति बनी। ओजोन परत सूर्य से आने वाले हानिकारक पराबैंगनी (UV) विकिरण को अवशोषित करती है, जिससे पृथ्वी पर जीवन की रक्षा होती है।

questions.text: किस प्रकार का श्वसन अधिक ऊर्जा प्रदान करता है और क्यों?
questions.text_english: What kind of respiration provides more energy and why ?

key_points: Aerobic respiration provides more energy.
It completely oxidises glucose in the presence of oxygen to produce CO2 and water, releasing 38 molecules of ATP per glucose molecule.
Anaerobic respiration only partially breaks down glucose and produces only 2 molecules of ATP.

questions.solution: Aerobic respiration provides much more energy than anaerobic respiration. In aerobic respiration, glucose is completely oxidised in the presence of oxygen to produce carbon dioxide, water, and a large amount of energy — approximately 38 molecules of ATP per molecule of glucose. In contrast, anaerobic respiration occurs in the absence of oxygen and only partially breaks down glucose, yielding lactic acid (in muscles) or ethanol and CO2 (in yeast), releasing only about 2 molecules of ATP. Since aerobic respiration achieves complete oxidation of glucose, it releases significantly more energy.

questions.solution: The three blanks are filled as follows: (i) Fish have a two-chambered heart (one atrium and one ventricle), and they have single circulation where blood passes through the heart only once per circuit. (ii) Amphibians such as frogs have a three-chambered heart with incomplete double circulation, where oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix in the ventricle. (iii) Birds and mammals have complete double circulation, meaning the blood passes through the heart twice in one full circuit, keeping oxygenated and deoxygenated blood completely separate. Complete double circulation, as seen in birds and mammals, is the most efficient type because it ensures the body tissues always receive fully oxygenated blood.

questions.text_english: In xylem tissue, vessels and tracheids of the roots, stems and leaves are interconnected to form a continuous system of water-conducting channels reaching all parts of the plant. Explain how this is achieved.

key_points: Water absorption by roots through osmosis and root pressure creates a push.
Transpiration pull — evaporation of water from leaves creates a negative pressure (suction) that pulls water upward through the xylem.
Cohesion-tension theory — water molecules stick to each other (cohesion) and to the walls of xylem (adhesion), forming a continuous water column that is pulled upward.

questions.solution: The continuous transport of water through xylem is achieved by the combined action of root pressure and transpiration pull. Roots absorb water from the soil through osmosis, and this creates a root pressure that pushes water upward into the xylem. More importantly, the leaves continuously lose water through transpiration — the evaporation of water from stomata. This creates a suction force called transpiration pull that pulls water up through the xylem vessels and tracheids. The water molecules hold together through cohesion (attraction between water molecules) and adhere to the xylem walls (adhesion), forming an unbroken water column from roots to leaves. The interconnected vessels and tracheids in roots, stems, and leaves form a continuous highway that allows water to travel from the soil to the topmost leaves of even tall plants.

questions.text_english: Show the cross and observations made by Mendel when he crossed pure tall pea plant with a pure short pea plant to get F1 progeny.

key_points: Parent cross: TT (pure tall) x tt (pure short)
All F1 plants are Tt (hybrid tall) — 100% tall plants
Mendel observed that tallness is dominant over dwarfness (shortness), as all F1 progeny appeared tall.
The trait 'shortness' appeared to disappear in F1 — it was called the recessive trait.

questions.solution: Mendel crossed a pure tall pea plant (TT) with a pure dwarf (short) pea plant (tt). The cross can be shown as: P generation: TT (pure tall) × tt (pure dwarf). The gametes produced are T (from tall parent) and t (from dwarf parent). In F1 generation, all offspring receive one T allele and one t allele, giving the genotype Tt. All F1 plants were observed to be tall. Mendel's observation was that the trait of tallness completely dominated over dwarfness — not a single dwarf plant appeared in F1. He concluded that tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t), which is recessive. The allele for dwarfness did not disappear but was merely masked in F1 generation.

key_points: (i) The structure shown is a Bryophyllum leaf with adventitious buds; the type of reproduction is vegetative propagation (asexual reproduction).
(ii) Advantage: Offspring are genetically identical to the parent, preserving desirable traits. Disadvantage: No genetic variation, so the population cannot adapt to environmental changes.

(iii) In asexual reproduction, a single parent divides/reproduces through mitosis, producing genetically identical offspring (clones). No fusion of gametes occurs, so no new gene combinations are created.

sub_questions.solution: The structure shown in the diagram is a Bryophyllum (or Kalanchoe) leaf bearing adventitious buds at its marginal notches. This is an example of vegetative propagation, which is a type of asexual reproduction. One advantage of this method is that it rapidly produces a large number of offspring that are genetically identical to the parent and carry all its desirable traits without requiring seeds. One disadvantage is that since all offspring are genetically identical (clones), there is no genetic diversity, making the entire population vulnerable to the same disease or environmental change. Asexual reproduction lacks genetic variation because it involves only one parent and reproduction occurs through mitotic cell division — producing daughter cells with exactly the same genetic material as the parent. There is no mixing of genetic information from two different individuals. Higher organisms have favoured sexual reproduction despite its complexity because it produces genetic variation through meiosis and random fertilisation of gametes. This genetic diversity allows populations to adapt to changing environments, fight off new diseases, and evolve over generations, improving the long-term survival of the species.

questions.text_english: Which of the following is an example of a displacement reaction ?

options.B: अभिक्रियाशील धातु की तनु अम्ल के साथ अभिक्रिया
options.D: बिना बुझे चूने की जल के साथ अभिक्रिया

options_english.B: The reaction of a reactive metal with dilute acid
options_english.D: The reaction of quick lime with water

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) — the reaction of a reactive metal with dilute acid. In a displacement reaction, a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its compound. When a reactive metal such as zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid, the zinc displaces hydrogen from the acid: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2↑. Combustion of natural gas is a combination/oxidation reaction. Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The reaction of quick lime (CaO) with water is a combination reaction (CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2). Only option (B) involves one element displacing another from a compound.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। अभिक्रियाशील धातु जैसे जिंक, तनु अम्ल से हाइड्रोजन को विस्थापित कर देती है: Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2↑। यह विस्थापन अभिक्रिया का उदाहरण है।

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — Copper(II) chloride, which is blue-green in colour. When copper(II) oxide (CuO, black solid) reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, the following reaction takes place: CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O. Copper(II) chloride (CuCl2) is the product and it dissolves in water to give a blue-green coloured solution. This colour change from black (CuO) to blue-green (CuCl2 solution) is the observed change. Option (A) is the reactant, not a product. Option (B) is incorrect as CuCl (Copper I chloride) is white, not blue. Option (D) is not formed in this reaction.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित समीकरण x KI + H2O2 → I2 + y KOH में x तथा y क्रमश: हैं:
questions.text_english: In the following equation x KI + H2O2 → I2 + y KOH, x and y respectively are :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) — x = 2, y = 2. To balance the equation 2KI + H2O2 → I2 + 2KOH: On the left side there are 2 K atoms, 2 I atoms, 2 H atoms, and 2 O atoms. On the right side, I2 provides 2 I atoms, and 2KOH provides 2 K atoms, 2 O atoms, and 2 H atoms. Both sides are balanced with x = 2 and y = 2. This reaction is a redox reaction in which iodide (I⁻) is oxidised to iodine (I2) and H2O2 is reduced to OH⁻.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है — x = 2, y = 2। संतुलित समीकरण: 2KI + H2O2 → I2 + 2KOH। दोनों पक्षों पर K=2, I=2, H=2, O=2 हैं।

questions.text_english:
Consider the structures 'X' and 'Y' given below:
X = n-butane (4 carbon straight chain) and Y = isobutane (branched 4 carbon)
Which of the following statements are correct ?
(i) 'X' and 'Y' are homologues.
(ii) 'X' and 'Y' have the same structural formula, but different molecular formula.
(iii) 'X' and 'Y' have the same molecular formula, but different structural formula.
(iv) 'X' and 'Y' are structural isomers.
questions.image_description: Structure X shows a straight-chain 4-carbon alkane (n-butane): H-C-C-C-C-H with all hydrogens shown (C4H10). Structure Y shows a branched 4-carbon alkane (isobutane/2-methylpropane): a central carbon bonded to three CH3 groups and one H (also C4H10).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) — (iii) and (iv). Structure X is n-butane (C4H10) — a straight chain of 4 carbons. Structure Y is isobutane/2-methylpropane (C4H10) — a branched structure. Both X and Y have the same molecular formula (C4H10) but different structural arrangements, confirming that statement (iii) is correct. Because they have the same molecular formula but different structures, they are structural isomers — confirming statement (iv). Statement (i) is wrong because homologues differ by CH2 in molecular formula; X and Y have the same formula. Statement (ii) is wrong because their molecular formulae are the same, not different.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। X (n-ब्यूटेन) और Y (आइसोब्यूटेन) दोनों का आण्विक सूत्र C4H10 है परन्तु संरचनात्मक सूत्र भिन्न है। अतः ये संरचनात्मक समावयव हैं।

questions.text_english: The reaction of calcium with cold water is :

options.A: कम तीव्र, लेकिन उत्सर्जित ऊष्मा हाइड्रोजन के प्रज्वलित होने के लिए पर्याप्त होती है।
options.B: अति तीव्र और ऊष्माक्षेपी तथा हाइड्रोजन प्रज्वलित हो जाती है।
options.C: ऊष्माक्षेपी, लेकिन उत्सर्जित ऊष्मा हाइड्रोजन के प्रज्वलित होने के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं होती है।

options_english.B: Very violent and exothermic and hydrogen catches fire.
options_english.C: Exothermic, but the heat evolved is not sufficient for the hydrogen to catch fire.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — Exothermic, but the heat evolved is not sufficient for hydrogen to catch fire. Calcium reacts with cold water to produce calcium hydroxide and hydrogen gas: Ca + 2H2O → Ca(OH)2 + H2↑. The reaction is exothermic (heat is released). However, unlike sodium and potassium which react very vigorously and the heat generated is enough to ignite hydrogen, calcium's reaction is less violent — the heat evolved is not sufficient to ignite the hydrogen gas produced. Option (A) is incorrect because the heat is not enough to ignite hydrogen. Option (B) describes the reaction of sodium or potassium with water.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। Ca + 2H2O → Ca(OH)2 + H2↑। यह अभिक्रिया ऊष्माक्षेपी है परन्तु उत्सर्जित ऊष्मा H2 को प्रज्वलित करने के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं होती। सोडियम और पोटैशियम के विपरीत, कैल्शियम की अभिक्रिया कम तीव्र होती है।

questions.text: किस स्थिति/स्थितियों में बल्ब जलेगा यह मानते हुए कि विद्युत परिपथ के अन्य सभी संयोजन पूर्ण एवं कार्यरत हैं? [चित्र में तीन बीकर दर्शाए गए हैं: (i) ग्लूकोज विलयन, (ii) ऐल्कोहॉल विलयन, (iii) तनु HCl]
questions.text_english: In which case/cases will the bulb glow considering that all other connections of electric circuit are complete and working ? [Three beakers are shown: (i) Glucose solution, (ii) Alcohol solution, (iii) Dilute HCl]
questions.image_description: Three circuit diagrams showing a battery, bulb, switch, and beaker with iron nails dipped in different solutions: (i) Glucose solution with iron nails and rubber cork, (ii) Alcohol solution, (iii) Dilute HCl. The bulb glows only when the solution conducts electricity (i.e., contains free ions).
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) — Case (iii) only. The bulb glows only when the solution in the beaker conducts electricity, which requires the presence of free ions. Glucose solution (case i) does not ionise in water — glucose is a covalent compound and its solution does not contain free ions, so it does not conduct electricity and the bulb will not glow. Alcohol solution (case ii) is also a non-electrolyte — alcohol does not ionise in water, so it does not conduct electricity. Dilute HCl (case iii) ionises completely in water to give H⁺ and Cl⁻ ions: HCl → H⁺ + Cl⁻. These free ions conduct electricity, completing the circuit and making the bulb glow.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है — केवल स्थिति (iii)। ग्लूकोज और ऐल्कोहॉल के विलयन में आयन नहीं होते, इसलिए वे विद्युत के चालक नहीं हैं। तनु HCl आयनित होकर H+ और Cl- देता है, जो विद्युत प्रवाह करते हैं, इसलिए बल्ब जलता है।

questions.text: जब जिंक NaOH के साथ अभिक्रिया करता है, तो निर्मित उत्पाद है:
questions.text_english: When zinc reacts with NaOH, the product formed is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — Na2ZnO2 (sodium zincate). Zinc is an amphoteric metal, meaning it can react with both acids and bases. When zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide (NaOH) solution, the following reaction takes place: Zn + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 + H2↑. Sodium zincate (Na2ZnO2) and hydrogen gas are formed. Na2O is sodium oxide and is not formed in this reaction. ZnO is zinc oxide — it forms when zinc burns in air, not when it reacts with NaOH. Zn(OH)2 is zinc hydroxide, which could form in certain conditions but is not the main product of Zn with NaOH.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। जिंक उभयधर्मी धातु है। Zn + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 + H2↑। सोडियम जिंकेट (Na2ZnO2) और हाइड्रोजन गैस बनती है।

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : कार्बन के यौगिक बड़ी संख्या में हैं, जिनमें बहुत से कार्बन परमाणु आपस में एक-दूसरे से जुड़े होते हैं।

questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : There are large number of compounds with many carbon atoms linked to each other.
Reason (R) : Carbon-Carbon bond is very strong and stable.
questions.instruction_line: दो कथन दिए गए हैं — जिनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को कारण (R) के रूप में अंकित किया गया है।
questions.instruction_line_english: Two statements are given — one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) — Both Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. The assertion is true: carbon forms an exceptionally large number of compounds (more than any other element), because carbon atoms can link to each other in long chains, branched chains, and rings. The reason is also true and directly explains this: the carbon-carbon (C-C) bond is very strong (bond energy approximately 347 kJ/mol) and stable, which makes it possible for carbon atoms to form long stable chains and networks, leading to the vast diversity of organic compounds. This property of carbon is called catenation.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सत्य हैं और कारण अभिकथन की सही व्याख्या करता है। C-C आबंध अत्यंत प्रबल और स्थायी होता है (श्रृंखलन गुण), इसलिए कार्बन बड़ी संख्या में यौगिक बनाता है।

questions.text:
संयोजी परमाणुओं के मध्य इलेक्ट्रॉनों के स्थानांतरण द्वारा निम्नलिखित आयनिक यौगिकों के बनने को दर्शाइए:
(i) सोडियम ऑक्साइड (Na2O)
(ii) मैग्नीशियम क्लोराइड (MgCl2)
[दिया गया है: परमाणु क्रमांक: Na = 11, Mg = 12, O = 8, Cl = 17]
questions.text_english:
Show the formation of the following ionic compounds by transfer of electrons between the combining atoms:
(i) Sodium oxide (Na2O)
(ii) Magnesium chloride (MgCl2)
(Given: Atomic number: Na = 11, Mg = 12, O = 8, Cl = 17)

key_points: (i) Na2O: Two Na atoms each lose 1 electron (2,8,1 → 2,8) to form Na+ ions; one O atom gains 2 electrons (2,6 → 2,8) to form O2- ion. 2Na+ + O2- → Na2O.
(ii) MgCl2: One Mg atom loses 2 electrons (2,8,2 → 2,8) to form Mg2+; two Cl atoms each gain 1 electron (2,8,7 → 2,8,8) to form Cl- ions. Mg2+ + 2Cl- → MgCl2.

questions.solution: For sodium oxide (Na2O): Sodium has electronic configuration 2,8,1 — it has 1 electron in its outermost shell. Oxygen has configuration 2,6 — it needs 2 electrons to complete its octet. Two sodium atoms each donate 1 electron to one oxygen atom. Each Na becomes Na+ (2,8) and oxygen becomes O2- (2,8). The electrostatic attraction between 2Na+ and O2- forms Na2O. For magnesium chloride (MgCl2): Magnesium has configuration 2,8,2 and loses 2 electrons to form Mg2+ (2,8). Chlorine has configuration 2,8,7 and gains 1 electron to form Cl- (2,8,8). One Mg atom donates its 2 electrons to two chlorine atoms (1 electron each). The attraction between Mg2+ and 2Cl- forms MgCl2.
questions.solution_hindi:
Na2O के लिए: दो Na परमाणु प्रत्येक 1 इलेक्ट्रॉन देकर Na+ बनते हैं। O परमाणु 2 इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करके O2- बनता है। 2Na+ + O2- → Na2O।
MgCl2 के लिए: Mg 2 इलेक्ट्रॉन देकर Mg2+ बनता है। दो Cl परमाणु प्रत्येक 1 इलेक्ट्रॉन ग्रहण करके Cl- बनते हैं। Mg2+ + 2Cl- → MgCl2।

questions.text: एक शुष्क क्वथन नली में 2 g हरे रंग के फेरस सल्फेट क्रिस्टलों को गरम किया गया। होने वाली रासायनिक अभिक्रिया के प्रकार का नाम लिखिए। अभिक्रिया के लिए संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण लिखिए। क्या यह एक ऊष्माक्षेपी अथवा एक ऊष्माशोषी अभिक्रिया है?
questions.text_english: 2 g of green coloured crystals of ferrous sulphate are heated in a dry boiling tube. Name the type of chemical reaction taking place. Write the balanced chemical equation for the reaction. Is this an exothermic or an endothermic reaction ?

key_points: Type of reaction: Thermal decomposition reaction.
Balanced equation: 2FeSO4 (heat) → Fe2O3 + SO2 + SO3
It is an endothermic reaction because heat energy is absorbed to decompose the compound.

questions.solution: When green crystals of ferrous sulphate (FeSO4·7H2O) are heated, they first lose water of crystallisation, and on strong heating, the anhydrous ferrous sulphate decomposes. The type of chemical reaction is a thermal decomposition reaction — a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances on heating. The balanced chemical equation is: 2FeSO4 → Fe2O3 + SO2↑ + SO3↑. The colour of the crystals changes from green (FeSO4) to reddish-brown (Fe2O3), and the gases sulphur dioxide (SO2) and sulphur trioxide (SO3) with a choking smell are evolved. This is an endothermic reaction because heat energy must be continuously supplied (absorbed) to bring about the decomposition of ferrous sulphate.
questions.solution_hindi: हरे फेरस सल्फेट को गर्म करने पर ऊष्मीय अपघटन अभिक्रिया होती है। संतुलित समीकरण: 2FeSO4 → Fe2O3 + SO2↑ + SO3↑। क्रिस्टलों का रंग हरे से लाल-भूरा हो जाता है। यह ऊष्माशोषी अभिक्रिया है क्योंकि ऊष्मा अवशोषित होती है।

Attempt either (a) or (b):

(iii) Blue colour of Copper(II) sulphate crystals turns white on heating.

sub_questions.text:
कारण दीजिए:
(i) अम्ल के तनुकरण के लिए, जल में अम्ल मिलाया जाता है, न कि अम्ल में जल।

sub_questions.text_english:
Give reasons:
(i) For dilution of an acid, acid is added into water and not water into acid.
(ii) Dry HCl gas does not turn blue litmus red whereas dilute hydrochloric acid does.
(iii) Blue colour of Copper(II) sulphate crystals turns white on heating.

key_points: (i) Dissolving acid in water is highly exothermic. Adding water to concentrated acid generates intense heat suddenly, which can cause the mixture to boil and splatter, causing burns. Adding acid to water ensures gradual heat release in a large volume of water.

(ii) Acids show acidic properties only when they dissociate to produce H+ (H3O+) ions, which requires water as the medium. Dry HCl gas has no water to ionise in, so it cannot produce H+ ions and does not turn litmus red.
(iii) Blue copper sulphate crystals are CuSO4·5H2O (hydrated). On heating, they lose the 5 molecules of water of crystallisation and become anhydrous CuSO4 which is white in colour.

sub_questions.solution: The three reasons are as follows. First, when acid is mixed with water, the process is highly exothermic. Adding water to concentrated acid can produce a sudden intense burst of heat that may cause the solution to splatter dangerously. Adding acid slowly into water ensures the heat is gradually absorbed by the large volume of water, making the process safe. Second, acids can show their properties only when they ionise to produce H+ ions (hydronium ions), and ionisation requires water as the medium. Dry HCl gas has no water present, so it cannot ionise and cannot produce H+ ions; therefore it does not turn blue litmus red. Dilute HCl readily ionises in water: HCl + H2O → H3O+ + Cl-, and the H3O+ ion turns blue litmus red. Third, blue copper sulphate crystals are hydrated — CuSO4·5H2O. The blue colour is due to the five water molecules of crystallisation. On heating, these water molecules are driven off, leaving anhydrous copper sulphate (CuSO4), which is white in colour.

sub_questions.text_english:
Write the preparation of the following compounds with balanced chemical equation:
(i) NaOH by chlor-alkali process
(ii) Baking Soda
(iii) Plaster of Paris

key_points: (i) 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O → 2NaOH + Cl2 + H2 (electrolysis of brine)
(ii) NaCl + H2O + CO2 + NH3 → NaHCO3 + NH4Cl (Solvay process, NaHCO3 = baking soda)
(iii) 2CaSO4.2H2O → (heat at 373K) → 2CaSO4.H2O + 3H2O (or CaSO4·½H2O — Plaster of Paris)

sub_questions.solution: The preparations are as follows. First, NaOH is prepared by the chlor-alkali process, which involves electrolysis of brine (concentrated aqueous sodium chloride solution): 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O → 2NaOH + Cl2↑ + H2↑. Chlorine is evolved at the anode, hydrogen at the cathode, and NaOH is formed near the cathode. key_points: (i) Homologous series: a series of compounds with the same general formula, similar chemical properties, differing by CH2. C2H4 and C4H8 belong to the same homologous series (alkenes, CnH2n).
(ii)(I) CH3-CH2-OH + CH3COOH → CH3COOC2H5 (ethyl ethanoate/ester) + H2O. (II) C2H5OH + 3O2 → 2CO2 + 3H2O.

sub_questions.solution: A homologous series is a group of organic compounds that have the same general formula and functional group, similar chemical properties, show a gradation in physical properties, and each successive member differs from the previous one by a CH2 unit (14 mass units). Among the given compounds — C2H4 (ethene), C4H10 (butane), C3H4 (propyne), C4H8 (butene) — the two that belong to the same homologous series are C2H4 and C4H8, both being alkenes (general formula CnH2n). For reaction (I): CH3-CH2-OH + CH3COOH (acid catalyst) → CH3COOC2H5 (ethyl ethanoate) + H2O. This is an esterification reaction. For reaction (II): C2H5OH + 3O2 (burning) → 2CO2 + 3H2O. This is a combustion reaction. Micelle formation occurs because soap molecules are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain fatty acids. Each molecule has a long non-polar hydrophobic hydrocarbon tail and a polar hydrophilic carboxylate head. In water, the hydrophobic tails cluster together pointing inward away from water, while the hydrophilic heads point outward into the water. This arrangement forms a spherical cluster called a micelle, which can trap oily dirt in the centre.

options_english.B: Ammeter and voltmeter both in parallel
options_english.C: Ammeter in series and voltmeter in parallel

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — ammeter in series and voltmeter in parallel. An ammeter measures current and must be connected in series with the circuit component so that all the current flows through it. It has very low resistance to avoid changing the current. A voltmeter measures potential difference (voltage) across a component and must be connected in parallel with it. It has very high resistance so that negligible current flows through it, ensuring it does not alter the potential difference being measured. Connecting them the wrong way would give incorrect readings and could damage the instruments.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) — Ray 1 is Red and Ray 2 is Violet. When white light passes through a prism, it undergoes dispersion into its constituent colours (VIBGYOR). Red light has the longest wavelength and the least refractive index, so it is deviated the least and emerges at the top (ray 1). Violet light has the shortest wavelength and the highest refractive index, so it is deviated the most and emerges at the bottom (ray 2). The order from least to most deviation is: Red, Orange, Yellow, Green, Blue, Indigo, Violet.

sub_questions.text_english: What happens when light is scattered from (i) very fine particles and (ii) very large size particles of medium ? Justify your answer in each case.

key_points: (i) Very fine (tiny) particles scatter shorter wavelengths (blue) more than longer wavelengths (red) — Tyndall effect. Scattered light appears blue.
(ii) Very large particles scatter all wavelengths equally — white light is scattered, and the object appears white (like clouds or foam).

sub_questions.solution: When light is scattered from very fine particles (particles much smaller than the wavelength of light), shorter wavelengths (violet and blue) are scattered much more strongly than longer wavelengths (red, orange). This is known as the Tyndall effect. The scattered light appears blue, which is why the sky appears blue — air molecules preferentially scatter blue light. When light is scattered from very large particles (much larger than the wavelength of light), all wavelengths of visible light are scattered equally, regardless of wavelength. The scattered light appears white. This is why clouds appear white — the large water droplets in clouds scatter all colours of light equally.

sub_questions.solution: A rainbow is a natural phenomenon that demonstrates the formation of a spectrum. It is formed when sunlight falls on water droplets suspended in the atmosphere after rain. Each spherical water droplet acts like a tiny prism. The sequence of events is: (1) White sunlight enters the water droplet and undergoes refraction, causing dispersion into its constituent colours (VIBGYOR); (2) The refracted light undergoes total internal reflection at the back inner surface of the droplet; (3) The reflected light again refracts upon exiting the droplet, further separating the colours. The combined effect produces a spectrum with violet at the inner arc and red at the outer arc of the rainbow. questions.solution: The eye defect shown in the diagram, where parallel rays converge in front of the retina, is Myopia (short-sightedness or near-sightedness). In this defect, the image is formed in front of the retina instead of on it. Two causes of myopia are: (1) the eyeball becomes too long (elongated), increasing the distance between the lens and the retina; and (2) the eye lens becomes too curved (excessive converging power), causing light to focus too early. Myopia is corrected by using a concave (diverging) lens of appropriate negative power. The concave lens diverges the parallel rays coming from a distant object before they enter the eye, so that the eye can now focus them exactly on the retina, restoring clear distant vision. (a) Name a device which is used to:
(i) Maintain a constant potential difference in a circuit.
(ii) Change the electric current in an electric circuit.
(b) When the potential difference between the terminals of an electric heater is 110 V, a current of 5 A flows through it. What will be the value of current flowing through it when the potential difference is increased to 220 V ?

key_points: (a)(i) Battery / cell / voltage source (बैटरी / सेल); (ii) Rheostat (धारा नियंत्रक)
(b) Resistance R = V/I = 110/5 = 22 Ω. New current at 220V = 220/22 = 10 A.

questions.solution: For part (a): (i) A battery (or cell or voltage source) is the device used to maintain a constant potential difference in a circuit. (ii) A rheostat (variable resistor) is the device used to change the electric current in an electric circuit by varying its resistance. For part (b): Using Ohm's law, the resistance of the heater remains constant. First, find the resistance: R = V/I = 110 V / 5 A = 22 Ω. Now, when the potential difference is increased to 220 V, the new current is: I = V/R = 220 V / 22 Ω = 10 A. So the current doubles when the potential difference is doubled, which is consistent with Ohm's law (I ∝ V at constant resistance).

questions.text_english:
Consider the given electric circuit:
[Circuit contains: 4Ω in parallel with (1Ω and 5Ω in series), then (5Ω and 3Ω in parallel), then 2Ω in series; 10V battery]
Calculate the following:
(a) Total resistance of the circuit
(b) The electric current drawn from the battery
(c) Potential difference between points P and Q

key_points: (a) Left parallel group: 4Ω || (1+5)Ω = 4||6 = 2.4Ω. Right parallel group: 5||3 = 1.875Ω. Total R = 2.4 + 1.875 + 2 = 6.275Ω ≈ 6.28Ω
(c) V(PQ) = I × (R_right parallel + 2Ω) = I × (1.875 + 2)

questions.solution: Analysing the circuit from the diagram: on the left side (between R and S), resistors 4Ω and (1Ω + 5Ω = 6Ω) are in parallel. Their combined resistance = (4 × 6)/(4 + 6) = 24/10 = 2.4Ω. On the right side (between P and Q), resistors 5Ω and 3Ω are in parallel. Their combined resistance = (5 × 3)/(5 + 3) = 15/8 = 1.875Ω. These two parallel combinations and the 2Ω resistor are all in series, so the total resistance = 2.4 + 1.875 + 2 = 6.275Ω (approximately 6.28Ω). The current drawn from the battery using Ohm's law: I = V/R_total = 10/6.275 ≈ 1.59 A. The potential difference between P and Q equals the voltage across the right parallel combination (5Ω || 3Ω) plus the 2Ω resistor: V(PQ) = I × (1.875 + 2) = 1.59 × 3.875 ≈ 6.16 V.

sub_questions.text_english:
(a) (i) What is a solenoid? Draw a diagram showing the magnetic field pattern due to a current-carrying solenoid (inside and outside).
(ii) Name any two factors on which the magnitude of the magnetic field due to a current-carrying solenoid depends.
(iii) A current-carrying solenoid is stretched and converted into a straight wire carrying current. Draw a diagram showing the magnetic field pattern around it and mark the direction of the magnetic field.

key_points: (i) A solenoid is a long cylindrical coil of wire with many closely wound turns. The magnetic field inside is strong and uniform (like a bar magnet), while outside it is weaker and non-uniform.
(ii) Two factors: (1) Number of turns per unit length; (2) The magnitude of current flowing through the solenoid.
(iii) When a solenoid is stretched into a straight wire, the magnetic field forms concentric circles around the wire, with direction determined by the right-hand thumb rule.

sub_questions.solution: A solenoid is a cylindrical coil consisting of a large number of circular turns of insulated copper wire wound closely and uniformly over a cylindrical surface. When current flows through a solenoid, it behaves like a bar magnet — the magnetic field inside the solenoid is strong, uniform, and parallel to the axis (similar to a bar magnet's field), while outside the solenoid, the field is much weaker and diverging from the ends. The field pattern inside shows parallel field lines, and outside it shows a pattern similar to the dipole field of a bar magnet. Two factors that determine the magnitude of the magnetic field of a current-carrying solenoid are: (1) the number of turns per unit length — more turns per unit length produce a stronger field; and (2) the magnitude of the current — a larger current produces a stronger field. When the solenoid is stretched into a straight wire, the magnetic field forms concentric circles in planes perpendicular to the wire. The direction of these circular field lines is given by the right-hand thumb rule: if the thumb points in the direction of current, the curled fingers show the direction of the circular magnetic field.

(I) What will be the direction of the force acting on the electron?
(II) What will happen to the direction of the force acting on the electron, if the direction of the magnetic field as well as the direction of motion of the electron, both are reversed?

key_points: (i) Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: hold the thumb, index finger, and middle finger mutually perpendicular; index finger = field direction, middle finger = current direction, thumb = force direction.
(ii)(I) Electron moves upward, field points left. For an electron (negative charge), use the reverse of Fleming's rule: force acts to the right (toward the viewer / out of page).
(II) If both the field direction and velocity are reversed, the force direction remains the same (two reversals cancel each other).

sub_questions.solution: A current-carrying conductor experiences a force when placed in a magnetic field. This is demonstrated by placing a conductor between the poles of a magnet and passing current through it. The direction of the force is given by Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: stretch the thumb, index finger, and middle finger of the left hand mutually at right angles. If the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic field (B) and the middle finger points in the direction of current (I), then the thumb points in the direction of the force (F) on the conductor. For part (ii): The diagram shows an electron moving upward and the magnetic field pointing to the left. For an electron (which carries negative charge), the force direction is opposite to what Fleming's Left-Hand Rule gives for positive current. Using F = q(v × B) for a negative charge, the force on the electron acts toward the observer (out of the page / to the right). For part (II): When both the magnetic field direction and the direction of motion of the electron are reversed simultaneously, the force from each reversal would be in opposite directions; however, since both are reversed at the same time, these two effects cancel each other out, and the direction of the force on the electron remains the same as before.
